subject: Staged evaluation & close playbook — commitments, ramps, and contract redlines
messages:
From: Marco Leone <cto@fintech.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation plan for Acme — initial ask

Hi Rafael / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Acme is lining up a staged evaluation and procurement cadence and I wanted to share what matters most to our side so we can align the MAP early. High level:

- Short POC (2–4 weeks) to validate latency & cost on our representative prompts
- Pilot (1–2 months) with a small committed spend to stress test ramp
- Production ramp to start after pilot sign-off with predictable pricing and a true-up mechanism

Procurement will insist on price protection and clear definitions of usage (they call out "billable tokens" vs. "inference requests"). Can you send a sample MAP + the commercial playbook you prefer (credits, commits, ramp tiers)? Also flag anything in standard T&Cs they'd likely redline (true-ups, audits).

Appreciate a tight timeline — we are aiming to decide vendor by mid-April.

Thanks,
Marco
CTO, Fintech.ai

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Leone <cto@fintech.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan for Acme — MAP draft attached

Marco —

Great context, thanks. I attached a first-pass MAP (MAP-Acme-v1.xlsx) and a short playbook outline below. Quick summary:

- Stage 0 (Eval/POC): 2 weeks, evaluation credits (waived unit cost up to 50k tokens), success criteria: latency < 200ms p50 and cost per 1k tokens within pilot target
- Stage 1 (Pilot): 6 weeks, nominal commit: $10k month equivalent, accelerate to Stage 2 on agreed metrics
- Stage 2 (Initial ramp): 3 months, committed spend $30k/month with ramp targets and 10% discount tier at $50k ARR commit

Commercial notes in MAP:
- True-up cadence: quarterly reconciliation with annual true-up for usage over committed levels
- Price protection: propose 12 months from effective date for committed units; we can include a limited CPI-based increase after 12 months
- Usage definition: billable tokens (generation tokens + prompt tokens) — we will provide sample tokenization mapping for Acme prompts

I've cc'd Neha to flag likely legal redlines (price protection language, audit language). Marissa — would you take the lead on the discount/commit proposal?

Attachments: [Attachment: MAP-Acme-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
From: Lydia Ramos <procurement@acme-corp.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Leone <cto@fintech.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan for Acme — MAP draft attached

Rafael —

Thanks for the draft MAP. A few procurement/legal items up front:

- Price protection: our legal team will want a hard floor on increases during the first 24 months (we typically push for 24 months). Can you confirm Redwood's stance?
- True-ups: we prefer annual true-ups only. Quarterly reconciliations create operational noise.
- Usage definitions: please confirm what counts toward billable units. We will push for exclusions (internal test tokens, CI/CD jobs).
- Audit & data residency: we will run this past security; please provide SOC 2 evidence and the audit workflow for usage reconciliation.

We can be flexible on ramp/commits if price protection and a clear true-up are in place. Legal has redlined a couple of license clauses — sending separately (License_Terms_redlines.pdf).

Regards,
Lydia Ramos
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp
procurement@acme-corp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Ramos <procurement@acme-corp.com>, Marco Leone <cto@fintech.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan for Acme — commercial structure suggestion

Lydia / Marco —

Appreciate the priorities. Proposed commercial structure (high level) to keep decision timeline tight while protecting both sides:

1) Evaluation / POC (2–4 weeks)
   - Evaluation credits (50k tokens) + technical support (2 sessions)
   - Success criteria captured in MAP worksheet (sample prompts)

2) Pilot (6 weeks) — optional commit
   - Minimum commit: $10k/month (billed monthly)
   - If pilot succeeds, apply $10k as credit toward Month 1 of Stage 2

3) Initial Ramp (90 days)
   - Commit band A: $30k/month (baseline) -> 5% discount
   - Commit band B: $50k/month -> 10% discount + 90-day price lock
4) True-up & Price protection
   - Suggested compromise: annual true-up (once per 12 months) with quarterly reconciliations used for operational alignment only
   - Price protection: 12-month price lock from signature on committed units; after 12 months price increases limited to CPI + 3% (cap 7%) — open to negotiation to 18–24 months if ACME needs longer protection
5) Audit & usage definition
   - Usage = billable tokens excluding internal CI/CD test clusters (we can mutually define a safe-harbor exclusion list)

Attached: Draft_SOW_Acme_v0.3.docx with the staged milestones and escalation path.

If procurement is comfortable, we can commit to a 60-day close timeline from SOW sign-off to executed contract — mapping MAP milestones to contract milestones keeps both teams aligned.

Next steps: Rafael to confirm final discount bands and Jordan to approve any non-standard price-protection concessions.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Draft_SOW_Acme_v0.3.docx (docx)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Acme — need guidance on true-up / price protection

FYI — forwarding the MAP thread. Procurement is pushing for longer price protection (24 months) and annual-only true-ups. We want to keep the close timeline tight (60 days) tied to MAP milestones.

Questions for leadership:
- Can we agree to a 12-month price lock with a CPI+3% cap? Procurement is likely to push back to 24 months.
- True-up cadence: Neha prefers annual only — is annual with quarterly operational reconciliations acceptable?
- Define "usage" defensibly: recommend "billable tokens" with a 15% safe-harbor for test/CI variance in year 1.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme — need guidance on true-up / price protection

Rafael / team —

Thanks for the summary. Recommended approach to keep the deal moving while limiting economics risk:

- Price protection: offer a 12-month guaranteed price lock on committed units. If Acme requests 24 months we can consider a 18–24 month extension in exchange for a higher commit band or a stepped discount (e.g., 12-month lock at 5% discount; 24-month lock requires commit band B).

- True-ups: agree to an annual contractual true-up, but include quarterly operational reconciliations as "informational" checkpoints (no billing adjustments at quarter level). Annual reconciliation drives billing adjustments.

- Usage definition: define "billable units" as billable tokens (prompt + generation). Provide a sample tokenization mapping for the most common Acme prompts. Include a safe-harbor: first 12 months allow a +/-15% variance for non-production test usage; after that revert to strict measurement.

- Timeline & MAP tie-in: MAP milestones become preconditions for contract execution (POC sign-off -> Pilot start -> Ramp start). Propose a 60-day close timeline from SOW sign-off; if legal needs more time, we accelerate procurement support.

If Acme pushes hard on 24-month price protection without increased commit, we should escalate for approval (I can approve a single concession of 18 months with executive sign-off).

Approve moving forward with Marissa's commercial bands and Rafael to propose the slightly stricter price-protection language (12-month lock + CPI+3% cap) in the next draft.

Jordan Blake
VP, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
